name: ScreenshotOne
tagline: Screenshot API for developers and agents.
shortDescription: ScreenshotOne turns URLs, HTML, and Markdown into screenshots, PDFs, rendered HTML, and website metadata through a documented API.
agentSummary: Agents can call ScreenshotOne directly, use the official CLI, use SDKs, or run the official MCP server to capture web pages for research, monitoring, QA, and visual evidence workflows.
bestFor: Website screenshots, PDF rendering, visual monitoring, Open Graph images, competitor research, and agent workflows that need browser-rendered page evidence.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Rendering arbitrary websites can involve rate limits, target-site blocking, CAPTCHAs, proxy behavior, copyright, privacy, and compliance concerns. Store API keys securely, use signed URLs before sharing screenshot links publicly, and review website terms before automated capture.
pricingSummary: Public pricing page with a free plan and paid monthly plans for higher screenshot volume.
authModel: API key scoped to a ScreenshotOne organization; keys can be sent as access_key or X-Access-Key.
accountCreation: Self-serve signup creates an organization and API keys in the dashboard.
browserSupport: Dashboard and Playground support browser-based setup and previewing screenshot options before API use.

capabilities.detail: Official CLI integrates ScreenshotOne into command-line workflows and is linked from the ScreenshotOne CLI integration page.
Screenshot API supports GET and POST requests to /take over HTTPS with URL, HTML, and rendering options.
Official MCP server lets LLM clients render website screenshots through ScreenshotOne.
ScreenshotOne Playground lets users test and preview screenshot API options in the browser before integration.
Docs describe self-serve signup, dashboard access, and API key creation.
Public pricing page lists free and paid ScreenshotOne plans.
Documentation covers getting started, API keys, request options, errors, SDK examples, webhooks, and related workflows.
No dedicated sandbox, test mode, local mode, or dry run is documented; Playground, Postman, CLI, MCP, and API calls use the live ScreenshotOne account and API quota.
